name: zip()
what_it_does: Pairs up items from two or more iterables position by position, so you can loop over them together instead of by index.
parameters: Two or more iterables of the same or different lengths.
return_value: A zip object yielding tuples, one per position, each combining the items from every input iterable at that position - usually unpacked directly in a for loop or converted with list().
example:
names = ["Ana", "Bob"]
ages = [25, 30]

for name, age in zip(names, ages):
    print(name, age)
common_mistakes: zip() stops at the SHORTEST input - if the lists are different lengths, extra items in the longer one are silently dropped, not an error. zip() itself is a one-time iterator in Python 3 - wrap it in list() if you need to loop over the pairs more than once.
when_to_use: Looping over two or more related lists in lockstep, e.g. combining a list of names with a list of scores.
